name: Hotseat Turn Pass
description: Pass-and-play turn order for one screen. Owns whose turn it is, the seat order, and the end-of-turn handoff — including the brief pass-the-device beat that keeps the next player's hand and hidden information private from the last player's wandering eyes. Networked multiplayer is social.party_system's job; this component depends on party_system only for the roster it sequences and otherwise assumes everyone shares one machine. It owns turn order and the handoff. It does not own what a turn contains — rolling, moving, and resolving are requested by the active player and owned by dice, track, and spaces — and it does not own turn timers: utility.timer_system already counts down, and a second clock is a bug farm.

inputs.name: playerOrder
inputs.description: Player ids in seat order, drawn from the social.party_system roster. Required because turn order is the one fact this component exists to know.

inputs.name: handoffDelaySeconds
inputs.description: The privacy beat between turns: hidden information is cleared, the next player is named, then control passes. Zero is legal but reads as a glitch on shared screens.

inputs.name: allowTurnUndo
inputs.description: Whether the outgoing player may retract an ended turn before handoff completes. Off by default; take-backs in hotseat are a social contract, not a feature.

outputs.name: completedRounds
outputs.description: Full circuits of the seat order. Many board-game rules key off rounds rather than turns; both counts are kept so neither has to be derived.
